candidates.statement: Gateway /v1/checkout returns 502 because its downstream call to order:8000/v1/orders returns HTTP 500; the order service is the failing dependency, and gateway 502s are a propagated downstream server error rather than a gateway-local fault.
candidates.uncertainty: Order-side telemetry (order logs/traces/metrics) is absent, so the internal cause of the order 500 (db, payment, inventory) is not established.

report.explanation: Traces and logs show every gateway /v1/checkout 502 is preceded by a client call to order:8000/v1/orders returning 500, with matching correlation IDs. Gateway metrics show no server-side error series and low latency, so the 502 is a propagated downstream failure. The bounded candidate is http-500 originating at the order service; the specific internal cause requires order-side evidence.
missing_evidence: Order service logs/traces for the failing /v1/orders requests to identify the internal 500 cause
Order service metrics (error rate, latency, dependency outcomes) around the incident window
Postgres/payment/inventory dependency telemetry to rule out db-pool-exhaustion or downstream-latency at order
